title: Tenant burst credits, cgroup QoS and proactive eviction playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and implement a tenant-level burst credit system combined with cgroup-like QoS classes and a proactive eviction playbook to reduce noisy-neighbor interference on Dedicated GPU pools. This ticket captures the product requirements, runtime design, autoscaler integration, console controls, telemetry and a staged rollout. Goals: (1) provide predictable throughput guarantees for committed tenants while allowing safe short bursts for spiky workloads; (2) reduce tail latency impact from noisy neighbors via early detection and soft-preemption; (3) provide operators with clear observability and recovery actions; (4) maintain cost transparency and billing correctness when burst credit allowances are used.
acceptance_criteria: Burst credit bucket per tenant implemented in scheduler with configurable capacity and replenishment rate
QoS classes (guaranteed | burstable | best-effort) enforceable at lane/host level and visible in Console
Proactive eviction workflow: soft-preempt -> checkpoint KV cache -> model unload -> fallback model applies within SLA targets
Autoscaler honors QoS classes: guaranteed tenants unaffected by background scaling of best-effort lanes
Dashboards show per-tenant credit balance, eviction events, and end-to-end latency regressions after bursts
E2E tests that simulate noisy neighbors demonstrate <10% P95 latency regression for guaranteed tenants
implementation_notes: Scheduler: add per-tenant token bucket (burst_tokens, refill_rate) persisted in etcd; token checks on request admission
Runtime: implement a soft-eviction API that asks a runtime to flush KV cache to warm storage and release model memory within X seconds
Kernel/Allocation: leverage existing lane fencing primitives but add a QoS label and per-lane priority multiplier
Autoscaler: extend policy to accept QoS-aware target calculations; do not scale down nodes hosting active guaranteed lanes unless forced by safety policy
Billing: annotate usage records with 'burst_used' flag and report to billing pipeline; create a flag to bill burst consumption at discounted rate or reallocate to monthly reserved bucket
Console: new tenant settings panel with sliders for burst capacity and refill rate and hard quota toggle
telemetry_and_alerts: Burst consumption event logs with reason tags (spike, stuck-requests, abusive-behavior)
Eviction events emitted with context: tenant, lane, model, KV cache size, estimated recovery time
Alert: sustained credit_ratio < 0.1 for > 2min for guaranteed tenants -> page SRE
Alert: >5 evictions in 10 minutes across a host -> trigger host-level noisy-neighbor policy
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): enable burst accounting and QoS labels on internal dev clusters; validate token accounting and dashboards
Phase 1 (early customers): opt-in for a small set of Dedicated tenants; observe impact on latency and billing reconciliation
Phase 2 (gradual): enable automatic soft-eviction for best-effort lanes only; default QoS mapping applied to new Dedicated pools
Phase 3 (global): enable hard quota enforcement for customers who enabled hard-quota toggle; document billing and SLA effects
Rollback: toggle QoS label to 'best-effort' and rehydrate cached models from snapshot; revert autoscaler policy to pre-change configuration
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: incorrect token accounting causing inadvertent throttling of guaranteed tenants -> Mitigation: conservative default refill rates and two independent token audits during canary
Risk: soft-eviction causes high tail latency during checkpoint -> Mitigation: stagger soft-evictions and enforce per-host eviction rate limits
Risk: billing disputes over burst consumption -> Mitigation: provide per-tenant, per-request evidence in billing UI and delayed reconciliation window
Risk: autoscaler misinterprets transient bursts as sustained demand -> Mitigation: add smoothing window and QoS-aware thresholds to scaling signals
